sections.h2: Who does what in McDuffie County
sections.html:
Three separate bodies touch a McDuffie County tax bill. The Board of Assessors, working out of the Tax Assessor's Office, judges taxability, value and equalization. Billing, collecting and passing money to other governments belong to the Tax Commissioner. When the assessors will not budge, the Board of Equalization, a citizen panel appointed by the Grand Jury, hears the dispute.

Reach the assessors at 706-595-2128, in person weekdays 8 am to 5 pm. That office sets values only, so a question about a statement goes to the commissioner. Returns are also filed with the assessors.

  • Value, returns, exemptions and homestead filings: the Tax Assessor's Office.
  • Statements, payments, liens and excess funds: the Tax Commissioner.
  • Millage: voted each year by the county commissioners and the school board, so neither tax office controls it.
  • A rejected appeal: Board of Equalization or arbitration, then Superior Court.

Budget and millage hearings meet at the McDuffie County Government Center, 210 Railroad Street, Thomson.

McDuffie County is a small, steady county in the Augusta metro area, west of Columbia and Richmond counties, with Thomson as the seat and Dearing the only other town. Interstate 20 crosses it along with US 78, US 221 and US 278, which helps commuters. The population was 21,640 in July 2025, almost the same as the 2020 base of 21,628.

The county has 9,725 housing units, 65.0 percent of them owner-occupied. The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $170,200 and rents run around $792. Builders pulled 86 permits during 2025.

sections.h2: Bills, due dates and late fees
sections.html:
McDuffie runs one of the earlier schedules in Georgia, with a mailing by September 15 and a November 15 deadline, five weeks ahead of the December 20 default used in other counties.

Dates and charges on a McDuffie bill
EventRule
MailingBy September 15
DeadlineNovember 15
InterestCharged monthly from the 16th, prime rate plus 3 divided by 12
Penalty5 percent each 120 days, topping out at 20 percent
FIFA tax lienFiled with the Clerk of Court 30 days after the bill is delinquent
Mobile homesMailed in January, due April 1

For a seller the lien is the problem. It shows on your credit report and in the public record, so clear the bill before the 30 days are up and the title search stays simple.

Installments are possible. The Tax Commissioner must approve a signed agreement set up before the bill goes delinquent. Ask for the agreement in writing and keep a copy with your closing papers.

The separate fire fee ends, with FLOST sales tax revenue taking its place. The county proposed a rate of 7.998 mills, compared with 7.809 mills in 2025, to absorb the fire cost. Ask the Tax Commissioner for the final rate that applies to your bill.

A Notice of Property Tax Increase may arrive even when the typical homestead bill drops. The comparison is to the rollback rate, shown as 6.085 mills for 2026, and it ignores the fire fee. City and school taxes, 15.124 mills in the estimator, are billed separately.

Buyers sometimes ask whether the lower homestead bill carries over to them. It does not follow the house, because each owner has to file for the exemption. Homesteads also get a one-time state credit. The Tax Commissioner describes it as $18,000 off assessed value, applied automatically when the homestead was filed on time.

sections.h2: How to appeal a new value
sections.html:
Count 45 days from the date on the notice of assessment. An appeal that arrives later is invalid, and it has to be in writing, delivered to the Board of Assessors.

The assessors look again and either adjust the value or send the file to the Board of Equalization, where each side states its position. The loser may go to McDuffie County Superior Court. Arbitration is available in place of the Board of Equalization if you choose it when you file.

  • Accepted grounds: taxability, uniformity and value.
  • Uniformity compares your value with similar properties.
  • Objecting to the size of the tax itself is not a ground.
  • Either the owner or the assessors can take a Board of Equalization ruling to court.

A denied homestead has its own path. The assessors decide eligibility, and a turned-down applicant must be told how to appeal.

File at the Board of Assessors Office from January 1 through April 1, having owned and lived in the house on January 1. The ordinary homestead exemption is $4,000. At 62 and older with net income under $15,000 it is $15,000, and at 65 and older there is $30,000 off assessed value for schools. Owners rated 100 percent disabled may use a local exemption with a doctor's documentation and the same income limit. After approval it continues without reapplying until ownership changes.

Land programs carry a ten-year covenant with the county:

  • Preferential agricultural property is taxed on 30 percent of market value in place of the usual 40.
  • Conservation use values land by what it produces now.
  • Environmentally sensitive property stays in its natural state under state rules.
  • Residential transitional property sits in an area changing to another use.

Timber is taxed one time, at 100 percent of fair market value, when cut or sold. A deferral is also available for homestead owners 62 and older with income of $15,000 or less, usually lasting until ownership changes.

Phone the Tax Commissioner for the full balance, including interest and any lien charge, and ask how the payoff reaches your closing attorney. A bill a few days late looks nothing like one stacked with penalty layers and a recorded lien.

  1. Get the balance in writing.
  2. Pay it at or before closing so no lien is recorded.
  3. Ask whether any older parcel or account is still open.

The office takes cash, checks, money orders and credit or debit cards, with fees on cards and no American Express. If land once sold at a delinquent tax sale left money over, claim it in writing with proper ID. The county has a list and an application.

For a mobile home, deal with the April 1 bill first, because it is an account separate from the land.

Before you list, pull your latest notice of assessment and your bill, and check the homestead filing is on record with the Board of Assessors. If you are close to the 45 day appeal window, file first and sort out the sale price later, because a missed window cannot be reopened. At closing, the attorney will want the commissioner's payoff in hand, plus proof that any installment agreement is current. A cash buyer can close quickly, so ask for the balance early enough that interest has not grown by the time the funds move.

faqs.q: What day are McDuffie County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Plan on November 15, with bills out by September 15, which is earlier than the December 20 default in other counties. Mobile homes follow an April 1 deadline.

faqs.q: How long can I appeal a McDuffie County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice date. The appeal must be written, and a late filing is treated as invalid.

faqs.q: What does it cost to pay a McDuffie County bill late?
faqs.a: Interest builds monthly from the 16th and a 5 percent penalty lands every 120 days up to 20 percent. A tax lien follows once the bill has been delinquent for 30 days.

faqs.q: Is the McDuffie County fire fee gone?
faqs.a: Yes, FLOST revenue replaces it, and the county rate was proposed at 7.998 mills. Ask the Tax Commissioner for the final rate.

faqs.q: Where does a McDuffie County homeowner apply for homestead?
faqs.a: At the Board of Assessors Office, between January 1 and April 1. The assessors handle and approve every exemption application.
